Read an AOEF file

Source: R/aoef.R
readAOEF.Rd

Reads the annotations held in a file in the Acoustic Objects Exchange Format (AOEF), the JSON format of the soundevent Python package, in which the Whombat annotation tool (Balvanera et al. 2023) exports its projects. The predictions of a model run are read in the same way.

Usage

readAOEF(file, audio.dir = NULL, output = "Annotation")

Arguments

file

Path to the AOEF file.

audio.dir

The directory the paths of the recordings in the file are relative to, as soundevent's audio_dir is. Where it is NULL the paths are given as the file has them.

output

One of "Annotation" or "data.frame".

Value

A list of Annotation objects, or a data frame if output is "data.frame".

Details

AOEF gives each sound event a shape: a stretch of time, a box of time and frequency, a single moment, a single point, or lines and polygons drawn on the spectrogram. Each is read as the smallest range of time and frequency that holds it, which for a stretch of time or a single moment is every frequency.

A sound event can carry several tags, each a key and a value such as dwc:scientificName and Turdus merula, while an Annotation has one type and one value. So a sound event is read as one annotation for each of its tags, with the key as its type, or as one annotation with no type and no value where it has no tags. The tags of a clip, a part of a recording annotated as a whole, are read in the same way as annotations spanning the clip. A clip with no tags and no sound events, annotated as holding nothing, is read as one annotation with no type and no value, so that the absence is kept.

The metadata of each annotation holds who made it (created_by), when (created_on), its notes, the features measured of it, and for a prediction its score and the tag_score of its tag. Under aoef it also holds the identifiers and the exact shape that writeAOEF() needs to write it back as it was, and what the file said of its recording. Sequences of sound events are not read.

soundevent on Windows writes in the encoding of the locale rather than in UTF-8, so a file that is not UTF-8 is read as Windows-1252.

References

Balvanera SM, Mac Aodha O, Weldy MJ, Pringle H, Browning E, Jones KE (2023). “Whombat: An open-source annotation tool for machine learning development in bioacoustics.” doi:10.48550/arXiv.2308.12688 . 2308.12688, https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12688.
